sequences.description: Default role change + role omission: ensure mount-level default_role does not allow privilege escalation when role is omitted on login
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions from a JWT login that omits role must be bounded by the intended default_role at that time; changing default_role must not allow a token intended for a low-priv role to receive high-priv policies.

params.description: jwt mount for default_role confusion test

oracle_checks.violation_description: JWT login that omitted role was accepted after default_role changed to high-role, potentially granting unintended high privileges
JWT login that omitted role gained access to high/flag after default_role change (authorization binding violated)

sequences.description: Config change: remove claim constraints (empty bound claims) and re-authenticate to see if previously constrained role becomes overly permissive
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Removing claim constraints should not allow a token lacking required upstream intent (e.g., missing/incorrect tier) to gain permissions; if empty constraints are treated as allow-all unexpectedly, authorization binding is violated.

params.description: jwt mount for empty-constraints test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control user with tier=gold could not read tiered/only; setup invalid or policy binding broken
After claim constraints were emptied, a bronze token gained access to tiered/only (authorization binding violated by overly permissive role)

sequences.description: Audience list bypass attempt: role bound_audiences=['vault-app'] but attacker supplies aud as a list containing 'vault-app' plus an extra audience; should not grant access if Vault requires strict audience semantics.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed BrokerPolicy; a token with ambiguous/multi-audience aud should not be accepted to gain the role's policy unless audience validation is strict and unambiguous.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 audience list bypass

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login could not read aud-allow secret; setup invalid or policy not applied
Multi-audience token was accepted and granted access to aud-allow secret, indicating weak audience binding

sequences.description: Empty bound_claims object bypass: role uses claim_constraints to require tenant='A'. Admin mutates role to claim_constraints={} and attacker re-authenticates; should not gain access if constraints are required for authorization binding.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Removing claim constraints should not silently broaden authorization beyond intended upstream intent; if it does, attacker can obtain permissions without required tenant claim.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 empty bound_claims bypass

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control tenantA user could not read tenantA secret; setup invalid
Attacker without required tenant claim was accepted before config change; claim constraint enforcement missing
After claim_constraints were emptied, attacker without tenant claim gained tenantA secret access (authorization broadened unexpectedly)

sequences.description: Attack: attempt to escalate privileges by abusing claim_mappings to map an attacker-controlled JWT claim into the policy-bearing identity_claim, potentially bypassing intended principal binding and granting admin policy.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed BrokerPolicy(config). Even if a JWT contains extra claims, the role must not allow an attacker to map themselves into a privileged identity (e.g., 'admin') and gain access to admin-only secrets unless explicitly intended by role constraints.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 role/policy confusion test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control user logged in via user_role was able to read admin secret; role/policy binding failed.
Attacker used claim_mappings confusion (preferred_username->sub) to impersonate privileged identity and read admin secret; authorization binding violated.

oracle_checks.assertion: "admin-read" not in user_attacker_confusion_policies AND "admin-read" not in user_attacker_confusion_identity_policies
oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker session unexpectedly included admin-read policy (directly or via identity policies) despite using user_role.
Attacker could not read user secret; setup likely broken (expected user_role to allow users/* read).
